summary.name: Etsy Debriefing Facilitation Guide
summary.one_liner: An open-source guide from Etsy for facilitating blameless post-mortem debriefings, framing them as learning opportunities rather than fixing exercises.
keywords: nancy leveson engineering a safer world
how to run a postmortem meeting
use_cases: Preparing and facilitating a post-incident debriefing meeting
Training engineers to facilitate blameless postmortems
Exploring multiple perspectives on a software outage
Moving a postmortem beyond a single root cause
Developing organizational learning practices after incidents
summary.what_it_does: The page is an Etsy blog post introducing a Debriefing Facilitation Guide that Etsy open-sourced for running post-mortem meetings. It argues that debriefings should prioritize learning over fixing and that facilitators should ask open questions to gather diverse perspectives. It includes an illustrated example in which follow-up questions uncovered a UI readability problem behind a failed deployment. It also describes having several engineers draw their mental models of an architecture on a whiteboard to reveal gaps in understanding. The page links to the guide's repository but does not itself summarize the guide's contents in detail.
notable: Open-sourced by Etsy and published with a GitHub repository
Built on Systems Safety and Human Factors ideas such as the New View on human error
Includes a real (generalized) debriefing example showing how questions revealed a dashboard font issue
Critiques the idea of a single 'root cause' in incident analysis
caveats: The page is a blog post and does not detail the guide's full contents; those are in the linked repository
Pricing is not stated on the page beyond it being open-sourced
